fix(cli,mcp): keep live authorize alive through the OAuth flow (#281)

The connector authorize OAuth handshake timed out before the token was
persisted (#259). Two root causes:

1. The OAuth flow is driven lazily by the list_tools discovery request,
   which is bounded by the per-call tool_timeout (default 30s), not
   init_timeout. The prior fix widened only init_timeout, so a Robinhood
   face-scan sign-in (>30s) still tripped the handshake.
2. The 30s timeout was retried, and the retry opened a fresh client
   context that started a SECOND OAuth callback server on a new port,
   orphaning the sign-in the user had just completed.

Fix:
- cmd_live_authorize now raises BOTH tool_timeout and init_timeout to a
  configurable authorize deadline (VIBE_LIVE_AUTHORIZE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
  default 300s), raise-only so a larger user value is preserved.
- The authorize handshake runs a single non-retried list_tools attempt
  via build_mcp_tool_wrappers(..., max_list_tools_attempts=1), so a
  transient failure cannot spawn a duplicate OAuth flow.
- _run_with_retry takes a configurable attempts cap; runtime/registry
  callers keep the default 2 (one transient retry) unchanged.

Closes #259

fix(security): block CGNAT/mesh ranges in SSRF guard; close QQ media redirect-to-internal

Two SSRF gaps in the channel media-fetch path:

1. channels/utils._is_private only checked is_loopback | is_link_local |
   is_private. ipaddress.is_private is False for RFC 6598 shared address
   space (100.64.0.0/10 — the default Tailscale/mesh range), so those hosts
   passed validate_url_target and every channel (QQ, DingTalk, NapCat,
   Telegram, channelsui) would fetch them as media. Switch to
   `not addr.is_global or addr.is_multicast`, which blocks all
   non-globally-routable ranges uniformly and also closes an IPv4-multicast
   gap (is_global is True for multicast). Matches web_reader_tool._url_allowed.

2. qq._read_media_bytes validated media_ref once, then fetched with
   allow_redirects=True. media_ref is agent-controlled (from msg.media, which
   is routinely influenced by untrusted external content), so a public URL
   returning 302 -> http://169.254.169.254/... would be followed unchecked and
   the internal body uploaded as a media attachment. Set allow_redirects=False
   and fail closed on 3xx, mirroring napcat.py. (The separate inbound download
   at qq.py:618 fetches a trusted QQ CDN URL and is intentionally left as-is.)

Adds agent/tests/test_url_target_security.py covering both fixes. The central
guard (validate_url_target / _is_private) previously had no tests at all.

fix(mcp): cap get_market_data row output

Every row of every symbol was emitted, so the canonical "1 symbol,
1 year, daily" request (~251 rows) breached the MCP token budget and
had to spool to a file, defeating an inline data tool (P07).

head+tail window plus truncation metadata (rows/returned/truncated/
hint); symbols within the cap are unchanged (plain list, so small
queries are byte-identical); max_rows=0 restores the unbounded legacy
behavior. Columnar encoding and envelope de-duplication are broader

NEW agent/src/agent/candlestick_intent.py
- @dataclass CandlestickIntent(symbol, timeframe, limit, window)
- detect_candlestick_intent uses three AND conditions:
    (a) prompt mentions "candlestick"/"candlesticks"/"padrões de candle"
    (b) symbol detected (reuses _extract_symbol from Patch 3)
    (c) no blacklist token (backtest, strategy, swarm, RSI, MACD,

- Defaults: limit=60 (capped at 200), window=20 (capped at 200),
  timeframe=1d (with 1h/15m heuristic for completeness)

NEW agent/src/agent/candlestick_workflow.py
- class CandlestickWorkflowDispatcher (ROUTED_BY="candlestick_workflow")
- 5-step pipeline:
    1. detect_candlestick_intent -> None falls through
    2. registry.execute("get_market_data", {symbol, timeframe, limit})
    3. _persist_ohlcv -> <run_dir>/artifacts/ohlcv_<safe_code>.csv
       (csv module, no new dependency; date,open,high,low,close,volume)
    4. registry.execute("pattern", {run_dir, patterns:"candlestick",
                                     window})
    5. _compute_verdict over counts: bull-bear >= 3 -> bullish;
       bear-bull >= 3 -> bearish; bull==0 ∧ bear==0 -> no_clear_signal;
       else -> neutral
- Sanitises every error path via market_data_dispatcher._sanitize (reuse)
- Never invokes LLM, web_search, read_url
- Emits trace events in fixed order: router, tool_call(get_market_data),
  tool_result, workflow_step(persist_ohlcv), tool_call(pattern),
  tool_result, answer, end(routed_by=candlestick_workflow,
  iterations=0, verdict)

EDIT agent/src/agent/loop.py
- Imports CandlestickWorkflowDispatcher
- After MarketDataDispatcher.try_route, before the ReAct while-loop:
  CandlestickWorkflowDispatcher().try_route(user_message, registry,
                                            trace, str(run_dir))
  Same success/failure handoff to RunStateStore.

Risk level: 3
Justification: second pre-LLM dispatcher; behavioural surface is the
prompt class "candlestick analysis on <symbol>". Narrow — two new
modules, no tool changes, ten-line loop edit.

Evidence
- 28 new tests pass (12 intent + 13 workflow + 3 loop integration).
- Full unit suite: 130 passed (was 102 pre-PR, +28). Zero regression.
- SEALED Level 1 canary (PR #4) remains green inside the 130.
- No new external dependency (stdlib csv only).

Threat model
- Abuse: small LLM cannot compose load_skill + get_market_data +
  write_file + bash + pattern for candlestick analysis. Empirically
  confirmed on qwen2.5:7b, llama3.1:8b, qwen2.5:14b — all returned
  no verdict. Patch 5 replaces that orchestration with a deterministic
  workflow that uses the same tools the LLM was supposed to call.
- Fail-closed (3 layers):
  (a) get_market_data error -> sanitised error, pattern NOT called.
  (b) persist OHLCV error -> sanitised error, pattern NOT called.
  (c) pattern error -> sanitised error.
  Every failure short-circuits with status=failed, iterations=0,
  routed_by=candlestick_workflow. No LLM, no web tools.
- Logs permitted: intent symbol/timeframe/limit/window; workflow_step
  with relative path; verdict.
- Logs forbidden: raw exception text, absolute paths, payload bodies,
  user prompt content.
- Anti-regression: 28 unit tests pin intent decisions, workflow
  ordering, run_dir routing, verdict mapping, fail-closed behaviour,
  no-leak property, and trace event order.
- Residual risks:
  R1: Verdict threshold of 3 signals is arbitrary; neutral covers
      the gray zone. Tunable in a follow-up if empirically off.
  R2: Pattern tool aggregates over the whole window, not the most
      recent N candles. "Right now" is interpreted as aggregate.
  R3: Detector may false-positive on metaphoric uses of "candlestick".
      Mitigated by blacklist + symbol-required AND.
  R4: Run dir injection trusts the AgentLoop's own run_dir; no escape
      since pattern tool already applies safe_run_dir on its side.

fix(cli): inject a host session id into non-interactive runs

The research-goal tools are registered unconditionally and resolve their
session from the host runtime, so an entry point that calls _run_agent without
an id makes every goal call fail validation with "session_id is required" while
the run still reports SUCCESS. Reported for `vibe-trading run`; six of the seven
_run_agent call sites had the same omission, including cmd_session_chat, which
already received the session id as a parameter and simply never forwarded it.

Add _ensure_session_id, which builds a Session (whose id is populated at
construction) and persists it best effort, so a store or index failure still
yields a usable id rather than the empty string that caused the bug.
cmd_continue reuses one session across continuations so goals accumulate: a
session-backed run_id already is a session id, since sessions and their traces
share SESSIONS_DIR, so it is used directly; a plain run gets a derived id.
Re-registering an existing id is idempotent. The interactive REPL had the same
latent hole whenever _new_session returned None, and now falls back to an
unpersisted id.

Also align the MCP contract. All four MCP goal tools declared session_id
required while the in-process registry injects it and leaves it optional — the
opposite contract, which asked the model to invent an internal identifier it
has no way to know. session_id is now optional there too, defaulting to one
stable id per server process.

feat(backtest): portfolio risk x-ray core + agent tool (Portfolio Studio slice)

First slice of the Portfolio Studio roadmap item ("risk x-ray ... rest
Planned"): a pure-computation risk x-ray for weighted baskets, plus an
agent-facing tool that fetches closes through the standard loader
fallback chain.

backtest/risk_xray.py computes, over trailing returns only (no look-ahead
by construction): concentration (HHI / effective N / top-1 / top-3),
annualized and downside volatility, max drawdown with dates, historical
VaR + expected shortfall at 95/99, diversification ratio, and pairwise
correlation / beta vs an equal-weight proxy. Weights are validated and
renormalized with a warning; thin symbols fall out through a min-history
filter; every emitted float is finite-guarded so the payload always
survives json.dumps(allow_nan=False). Long-only for now — a short leg
changes concentration semantics and deserves its own slice.

The portfolio_risk_xray tool handles argument validation, shapes the
fetch envelope into a close panel (records with missing or mixed
timestamps fall back to loader order), and returns a strict-JSON
envelope with unresolved/skipped bookkeeping. Data fetching is
injectable for tests.

17 new tests cover the math on hand-built panels, the edge matrix
(renormalization, thin symbols, single asset, zero variance, bad
args), and the tool end to end with a stub fetcher. Full suite:
6037 passed, 12 skipped.

fix(cli): load ~/.vibe-trading/.env on the connector command path (#902)

`main()` routes the `connector` subcommand group straight to
`_dispatch_connector`, which — unlike the interactive TUI — never runs
preflight, so nothing populated `os.environ` from `~/.vibe-trading/.env`.
`EnvConfig` reads only `os.environ`, so every connector resolving
credentials through `get_env_config()` reported them as missing despite a
valid file on disk: Longbridge's app key / secret / access token (the only
broker credential set sourced from env vars rather than a JSON config
file), and Futu's `FUTU_TRADE_PWD_MD5` live-unlock hash.

Call the existing `_ensure_cli_env()` helper at the dispatcher entry.
`_ensure_dotenv()` is idempotent and loads with `override=False`, so a real
environment variable still outranks the file, and connectors that read JSON
config are unaffected.

Distinct from #477 / #541, which were the stale-`EnvConfig`-singleton
variant: there `_ensure_dotenv()` ran but no `reset_env_config()` followed.
Here it never ran at all, so that fix could not reach this path.

Closes #901

chore(deps): unblock the ccxt/setuptools lock deadlock and cut dependabot churn

Dependabot could not land either half of a mutually-blocking pair: the
minor/patch group wanted ccxt 4.5.68 (which pins setuptools==83.0.0) while
keeping setuptools at 82.0.1, and the separate setuptools 83.0.0 PR conflicted
with the ccxt 4.5.67 already in the lock. Neither can go green alone because
setuptools is a major bump and is excluded from the minor/patch group by
design, so it cannot ride along.

Regenerate the lock so both move together. Verified with pip-compile under
Python 3.11 on Linux (matching CI) and checked with CI's own gate,
pip install --dry-run --require-hashes. Note the lock is platform-sensitive:
regenerating on macOS drops jeepney/secretstorage and swaps py-mini-racer for
mini-racer, so it must be produced on Linux.

Also ignore websockets, capped at <16 by langgraph-sdk 0.4.2, and move all
three ecosystems to monthly with 2 concurrent PRs. Security updates are a
separate channel and are unaffected.

fix(optimizers): exclude decision-bar returns (#487)

BaseOptimizer.optimize() built each estimation window with ret.loc[:dt], which
includes ret[dt] — a close-to-close return for the decision date. Since
weights at dt execute at that bar's open, ret[dt] isn't actually observable
yet at execution time, so every optimizer built on this base (mean-variance,
equal-volatility, max-diversification, risk-parity, turnover-aware) was
leaking one bar of future information into its own decision.

Fix restricts the window to ret.index < dt. Two regression tests prove it:
the window's latest timestamp always precedes the decision date, and shocking
only the decision-bar return leaves that bar's executed weights unchanged.
Backtests without an optimizer are unaffected; this does change historical
optimized results as intended (removing a look-ahead leak, not introducing
one).

Verified locally: full backend suite green (only 2 pre-existing/unrelated
failures, same as main), env-var CI gate passes, ruff clean, 18/18
optimizer-specific tests pass including both new causality tests.

fix(frontend): prevent insertBefore DOM race during streaming output

During streaming, the chat UI rendered two separate conditional blocks
(pre-stream placeholder and live streaming area) that mounted/unmounted
independently based on state transitions. When reasoningActive switched
to streamingText, React had to simultaneously unmount one div and mount
another, while scrollToBottom requestAnimationFrame inserted DOM
operations between React reconciliation cycles, causing the reference
node to disappear and triggering an insertBefore NotFoundError.

Fix by merging both blocks into a single stable wrapper div that only
checks status === streaming, with inner conditionals controlling
which content is shown. The wrapper itself never unmounts during
streaming, eliminating the DOM race.

Also debounce ConversationTimeline scroll handler DOM queries with
requestAnimationFrame to avoid conflicts with React batched updates.

fix(ibkr): reject NaN ticker values in _wait_for_tick

The _wait_for_tick loop checked `value is not None` before exiting,
but ib_async tickers return `float("nan")` for fields that have been
processed but contain no trade data (e.g. after-hours, illiquid
symbols).  Since NaN is not None, the loop exited immediately and
returned NaN bid/ask/last -- breaking all quote-dependent analysis.

  Only returns True when at least one of bid/ask/last is a non-NaN
  numeric value.
- _wait_for_tick now calls _tick_has_data() instead of inline None
  checks.
- Added test_quote_rejects_nan_and_waits_for_real_data -- mock returns

fix(shadow): skip the entry-hour gate on daily bars

Rules mined from real journals carry an entry_hour window from actual
fill times (p10-p90, e.g. 9-11 for market-hours trading). The generated
signal engine replays on daily bars stamped at midnight, so gating on
bar_hour rejected every bar: any profile mined from real intraday fills
produced a silently flat strategy with zero entries and no error.

information, so the generated engine now applies it only when the bar
index has more than one distinct time-of-day (intraday data). Other
rule conditions (RSI, prior return, holding) are unchanged.

fix(ibkr): use snapshot quotes and thread-local connection pool

## Problem

The previous shared-connection pool was incompatible with the agent's
parallel tool executor (ThreadPoolExecutor, up to 8 workers).  When the
agent fired 15 trading_quote calls in one iteration every worker thread
raced into the same `ib_async.IB` socket.  `ib_async` is not
thread-safe — its internal event loop is bound to one thread — so the
parallel access deadlocked the market-data stream.  Every session trace
ended with tool_call events but zero tool_result events for quotes.

Additionally, `get_quote` called `reqMktData` with `snapshot=False`
(streaming subscription) followed by a 2-second sleep and manual cancel.
This held the connection for 2+ seconds per symbol even when it worked.

## Solution

Two changes in `agent/src/trading/connectors/ibkr/local.py`:

1. **`reqMktData(..., snapshot=True)`** — requests a one-shot snapshot
   instead of a streaming subscription.  No sleep needed; the ticker
   delivers one tick and auto-cancels.  Drops the `_sleep(2.0)` and
   `cancelMktData` dance entirely.

2. **Thread-local pool** — replaces the shared `_TwsPool` with a
   `threading.local()`-based design:

   - Each worker thread gets its own `ib_async.IB` socket.
   - Unique client IDs via `itertools.count` + base config ID.
   - Per-thread reference counting so the connection persists across
     multiple tool calls in the same thread and disconnects only when
     the refcount drops to zero.
   - No socket is ever shared across threads — respects ib_async's
     single-thread-per-socket design.

## Impact

- No more hangs when the agent fires parallel trading_quote calls.
- Quotations complete in ~100 ms instead of 2+ seconds.
- All 10 `test_ibkr_local.py` tests pass without modification.

fix(agent): make Stop responsive mid-stream and between tools (#229) (#235)

Symptom 2 of #229: clicking Stop during a run did nothing, or only took
effect after a long delay. The cancel signal (_cancelled bool) was polled
only at the top of the ReAct iteration loop, so a Stop pressed while the
agent was mid-LLM-stream or executing tools was ignored until the entire
current iteration — the whole streamed answer plus all its tool calls —
finished and the next iteration check ran.

Add cooperative cancel checkpoints at the granularity the user actually
waits on:

- Switch _cancelled to a threading.Event (_cancel_event) so the flag is
  safe to poll from the streaming thread.
- Thread a should_cancel predicate into ChatLLM.stream_chat; the per-chunk
  loop breaks as soon as it is set, so a live stream stops at the next
  token instead of running to completion.
- After the stream returns, check the flag before processing tool calls:
  a cancel during streaming ends the run immediately and discards the
  partial turn (no tools run).
- Check the flag at the top of _process_tool_calls and between tool batches
  in _batch_execute, so a multi-tool turn stops after the current tool
  rather than launching the rest.

Limitation (documented in the PR): a connection that hangs before emitting
any chunk leaves the worker blocked in a socket read, which Python cannot
interrupt cooperatively from another thread; that case stays bounded by the
existing client timeout (TIMEOUT_SECONDS). Cancel now lands promptly in all
the normal "working" states (tokens streaming, tools running).

Tests: chat-level should_cancel breaks the chunk loop (and absence is a
no-op); loop-level cancel mid-stream ends the run as cancelled and skips
tool execution. Full suite: 3199 passed, 2 skipped.

fix(mcp): handle dataclass tool results in _make_jsonable (#849)

_make_jsonable only converted Pydantic BaseModel instances (via
model_dump), list, and dict. fastmcp's client auto-types
CallToolResult.data from a tool's output schema via
json_schema_to_type, which produces a plain stdlib dataclass (not a
BaseModel) whenever the schema doesn't set additionalProperties: true
-- the common case for a typical Pydantic-model tool return type. Such
an instance fell through to the final `return value` unconverted, so
json.dumps's `default` callback received the same unconvertible object
back and raised ValueError: Circular reference detected (its cycle
detector can't distinguish "default() gave up" from an actual cycle).

Adds a dataclasses.is_dataclass branch that recurses per-field (not a
raw asdict(), which would leave nested datetime/dataclass values
unconverted), plus a datetime/date branch, since a date-time schema
field validates to a real datetime object and would hit the same
failure one level down.

Reproduced against the real fastmcp dependency using an MCP tool's
output schema shaped like this (plain object properties, no
additionalProperties, nested datetime field): old _make_jsonable raises
the reported Circular reference detected error; the patched version
serializes correctly, verified both from direct construction and via
pydantic.TypeAdapter validation (the path fastmcp's client actually
uses).

fix(backtest): consume historical USD-M funding + round settlement jitter (#819)

Two fixes that make historical funding actually flow into perp backtests:

1. Loader: Binance funding settlement timestamps carry millisecond
   jitter (e.g. 2026-05-05T08:00:00.011Z). The raw timestamps never
   intersect bar timestamps, so the missing-settlement guard raises
   'funding settlement data is missing' for most real fetches. Round
   settlement timestamps to the second before aligning.

2. Engine: the loader writes a historical funding_rate column into the
   frame, but calc_crypto_funding_fee still charges the fixed config
   rate (default 0.0001) — the fetched data is never consumed. Prefer
   the bar's historical rate when present and finite; fall back to the
   fixed rate otherwise (spot-proxy and daily-fallback paths keep
   their existing behaviour).

Verified against live Binance USD-M data (BTC/ETH -USDT-PERP, 4H,
Jan-Jul 2026): fixed-rate short returned +44.5%, historical-funding
short +39.1% — the ~5pp delta matches 2026's predominantly negative
funding regime where shorts pay.

Tests: jitter alignment test in test_ccxt_perpetual_loader.py; three
override/fallback tests in test_crypto_engine.py.

fix(fundamentals): dedup restated rows and prevent period regression in PIT snapshots

Two point-in-time correctness bugs in tushare_fundamentals.py:

1. `query_fundamentals` did not deduplicate after the PIT cut, so the same
   (ts_code, end_date) could appear twice when both the original filing and a
   later restatement were visible as of the query date.  Fix: after the PIT
   cut, keep only the row with the latest effective pit date per
   (ts_code, end_date); ties preserve the last row in input order (natural
   Tushare ordering where restatements follow originals).

2. `enrich_price_frames_with_fundamentals` fed the deduped snapshot directly
   into merge_asof.  This caused two problems: (a) the per-day PIT visibility
   was evaluated on already-deduped data, making a restatement whose pit_date
   was in the future appear as if it were always visible; (b) when a late
   restatement for an *older* period (end_date < currently-visible end_date)
   arrived, merge_asof picked it as the nearest-prior announcement, regressing
   every subsequent snapshot to the older period.

   Fix: enrich now calls the new internal `_query_pit_cut` (raw PIT cut, no
   dedup) and builds an explicit forward-only effective timeline — a row is
   only accepted into the timeline when its end_date >= the currently-visible
   end_date.  Same-period restatements (same end_date, later pit_date) pass
   this check and appear as additional timeline entries; merge_asof then
   surfaces the restatement value only from its own pit_date onward.

Fixes #771

fix(backtest): make the buy-and-hold return path sign-safe

close.pct_change() silently assumes price[t-1] > 0. That holds for equities but
not for instruments that can print zero or negative prices, such as European
day-ahead power. As the divisor approaches zero an ordinary absolute move reads
as an enormous percentage move, so the compounded benchmark explodes — a
reported +39,560% where the honest figure was -42.7%. At exactly zero the next
bar is inf, which fillna(0.0) does not neutralise because it fills NaN, and
(1 + r).prod() then collapses to nan.

Adopt an explicit contract. A return is defined only when the previous price is
finite and strictly positive; otherwise it is 0.0, never inf or nan. Buy-and-
hold total return becomes the price relative P_end / P_start - 1 rather than the
compounded product, and is omitted entirely when the entry price is not
positive, because no honest percentage exists. Undefined bars are logged rather
than silently swallowed: a wrong return is a wrong reported number, not a crash.

bar_returns keeps the exact `close / prev - 1` expression pct_change uses, so
results for strictly positive series are bit-identical and ordinary equity and
crypto runs are unchanged.

The loader still rejects an exact-zero close, but the reason has narrowed to the
one that survives: sizing is target_notional / abs(price), undefined at zero.

Closes #872

chore(deps): ignore the transitive versions ccxt exact-pins

ccxt does not use ranges — it exact-pins its entire transitive closure. All 23
of those packages that appear in our lock sit at precisely ccxt's pin, with no
mismatches, so none can move until ccxt itself releases, and ccxt 4.5.68 is
already the latest. Any Dependabot PR touching one is unmergeable by
construction: the pip group PR proposed five of them and died with
ResolutionImpossible on certifi against the ccxt line in the lock.

Re-running the resolver confirms this is the ceiling rather than a stale lock —
pip-compile --upgrade under python:3.11-slim, matching CI, reproduces every one
of those versions, so there is no lock change to make. pydantic-core is in the
same position via pydantic's own == pin, and was the sixth package in that PR.

Ignore the set. ccxt itself is deliberately not ignored: it is the package whose
bump legitimately carries all of them. This suppresses only the automated PRs —
Dependabot alerts come from the dependency graph and are unaffected by this
file, so a CVE in cryptography, urllib3, requests or certifi still surfaces in
the Security tab, where the remedy is a ccxt bump.

fix(anthropic): self-heal models that deprecate the temperature field (#890)

Problem
-------
Next-gen Claude models (e.g. claude-opus-5, claude-opus-4-8, claude-sonnet-5)
reject the "temperature" request field with HTTP 400 "temperature is deprecated
for this model." for ANY value, while older models (claude-opus-4-5,
claude-sonnet-4-5, ...) still accept it. _build_anthropic unconditionally
forwarded the global default temperature=0.0, so every run on a next-gen model
failed before producing output. Model names are not predictable (opus-4-5
accepts it, opus-4-8 does not) and the rejection is value-independent, so
neither a fixed model allowlist nor an "omit when 0.0" shortcut is a correct
fix.

Solution
--------
Add a temperature-safe ChatAnthropic subclass (_make_temperature_safe_anthropic)
that wraps all four generation entry points (_generate, _agenerate, _stream,
_astream). When the API reports temperature as unsupported it drops the field
and retries once, then records the model in a process-wide set so subsequent
requests omit it up front (no repeated failed request). Models that accept
temperature keep their configured deterministic value unchanged. The subclass
is built from the lazily-imported class and cached per base class, preserving
the optional langchain-anthropic dependency boundary and existing test doubles.

Correct for any temperature value, current and future model names, and the
streaming path the Web UI relies on.

Tests
-----
Add regression tests in agent/tests/test_llm.py: self-heal retry drops
temperature and remembers the model, temperature is preserved for supporting
models, and the error matcher only triggers on temperature-unsupported errors.
Full test_llm.py suite: 58 passed.

fix(mcp): accept IPv6 and case-variant hosts in the network guard

The GHSA-p3c9 guard wrapped network MCP transports in Starlette's
TrustedHostMiddleware, whose plain split(":") Host parsing mangles
bracketed IPv6 ([::1]:8900 -> "[") and matches case-sensitively. An
MCP server bound to --host ::1 rejected every request with 400, and no
VIBE_TRADING_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS entry ([::1] or ::1) could fix it — the
only way out was '*', disabling the protection entirely. LOCALHOST was
rejected the same way, while the Origin guard (urlparse().hostname)
already lowercased, so the two layers disagreed.

Replace the middleware with a repo-owned _HostGuardMiddleware that
normalizes the header (brackets/port stripped, bare IPv6 kept whole,
lowercased) before matching the allow-list, normalize configured
entries the same way, and add ::1 to the loopback default. Allow-list
semantics (exact, *. wildcard, *) and the 400 rejection are unchanged;
the Origin guard is untouched.

Refs GHSA-p3c9

fix(mcp_server): pre-warm registry in main thread to avoid tools/call deadlock

_get_registry() lazy-imports src.tools.build_registry on first call. Every
caller is a FastMCP tool handler, so the first tools/call triggers the lazy
init inside FastMCP's asyncio worker thread, where the import chain (notably
src.tools.shell.*) deadlocks. initialize and tools/list succeed because
they don't touch the registry.

Pre-warming _get_registry() in main() — after _include_shell_tools is set
and before mcp.run() — performs the import on the main thread and lets
worker threads only ever read the cached singleton. _get_registry() is
idempotent (if _registry is None guard), so the 14 existing call sites are
unaffected.

fix(backtest): keep bar_returns bit-identical for gapped positive series (#895)

* fix(backtest): keep bar_returns bit-identical for gapped positive series

#872 replaced close.pct_change().fillna(0.0) with bar_returns and stated that
results for strictly positive series are bit-identical, so ordinary equity and
crypto runs are unchanged. That was verified only on gapless series.

On the pinned pandas (>=2.0,<3.0) pct_change defaults to fill_method='pad' and
forward-fills the divisor. bar_returns divided by the raw shifted series, so any
positive series with an interior NaN diverged. _align deliberately limits its
ffill to 5 bars (base.py:166-179) to keep long suspensions visible, so a halt
longer than that reaches bar_returns as a NaN prior and the real move across it
is reported as 0.0 -- silently, because the undefined-bar counter excludes NaN
priors by construction. On a real _align run an 8-bar halt turned a +17.1429%
resumed-trading bar into +0.0000%.

Injecting a zero where a large move occurred shrinks dispersion. Return deltas
cancel by sign; that damage does not. On a 20-symbol universe with two halted
symbols and news-shaped gaps, annualised vol fell 4.9619% -> 4.4673% and Sharpe
rose 3.0502 -> 3.3817.

Carry the prior price forward explicitly. This restores the pre-#872 answer and,
unlike the deprecated default it replaces, gives the same result on every
supported pandas -- the old behaviour flips silently under pandas 3.0, where
fill_method is None. The #872 contract is untouched: a non-positive prior is
still undefined, still 0.0, still logged.

Second, smaller item: inf > 0 is True, so where(prev > 0) kept an infinite prior
and the bar after it read as a clean -1.0 with no warning. buy_and_hold_return
had the same asymmetry -- it checked isfinite(last) but only first > 0, so an
infinite entry price returned -100% instead of None. Both now assert finiteness.

fix(anthropic): self-heal models that deprecate the temperature field (#890)

Problem
-------
Next-gen Claude models (e.g. claude-opus-5, claude-opus-4-8, claude-sonnet-5)
reject the "temperature" request field with HTTP 400 "temperature is deprecated
for this model." for ANY value, while older models (claude-opus-4-5,
claude-sonnet-4-5, ...) still accept it. _build_anthropic unconditionally
forwarded the global default temperature=0.0, so every run on a next-gen model
failed before producing output. Model names are not predictable (opus-4-5
accepts it, opus-4-8 does not) and the rejection is value-independent, so
neither a fixed model allowlist nor an "omit when 0.0" shortcut is a correct
fix.

Solution
--------
Add a temperature-safe ChatAnthropic subclass (_make_temperature_safe_anthropic)
that wraps all four generation entry points (_generate, _agenerate, _stream,
_astream). When the API reports temperature as unsupported it drops the field
and retries once, then records the model in a process-wide set so subsequent
requests omit it up front (no repeated failed request). Models that accept
temperature keep their configured deterministic value unchanged. The subclass
is built from the lazily-imported class and cached per base class, preserving
the optional langchain-anthropic dependency boundary and existing test doubles.

Correct for any temperature value, current and future model names, and the
streaming path the Web UI relies on.

Tests
-----
Add regression tests in agent/tests/test_llm.py: self-heal retry drops
temperature and remembers the model, temperature is preserved for supporting
models, and the error matcher only triggers on temperature-unsupported errors.

fix(cli): load ~/.vibe-trading/.env on the connector command path (#902)

`main()` routes the `connector` subcommand group straight to
`_dispatch_connector`, which — unlike the interactive TUI — never runs
preflight, so nothing populated `os.environ` from `~/.vibe-trading/.env`.
`EnvConfig` reads only `os.environ`, so every connector resolving
credentials through `get_env_config()` reported them as missing despite a
valid file on disk: Longbridge's app key / secret / access token (the only
broker credential set sourced from env vars rather than a JSON config
file), and Futu's `FUTU_TRADE_PWD_MD5` live-unlock hash.

Call the existing `_ensure_cli_env()` helper at the dispatcher entry.
`_ensure_dotenv()` is idempotent and loads with `override=False`, so a real
environment variable still outranks the file, and connectors that read JSON
config are unaffected.

Distinct from #477 / #541, which were the stale-`EnvConfig`-singleton
variant: there `_ensure_dotenv()` ran but no `reset_env_config()` followed.
Here it never ran at all, so that fix could not reach this path.

Add allow_nonpositive_prices: open on negative-price bars, still reject zero (#816)

Markets like European day-ahead power clear negative routinely, but the
loader's validate_ohlc drops any bar with a non-positive OHLC value and the
engine rejects any open at price <= 0. On real EU power data this silently
deletes ~27% of DE-LU days (every bar with a sub-zero hourly-derived low),
punching holes in rolling statistics (e.g. a z-score entry signal) with no
warning.

Add an opt-in `allow_nonpositive_prices` flag (default False — existing
behavior byte-identical for all positive-price markets):

- loaders/base.py: validate_ohlc gains the flag. Structural invariants
  (high<low, high/low bracketing open/close) always enforced; when the flag
  is set, negative prices pass through and only an exactly-zero price is
  rejected. Zero is genuinely undefined for `size = notional / price` and
  margin; a negative price is well-defined via abs().
- engines/base.py: BaseEngine reads the flag from config. _plan_open_order
  rejects an exactly-zero open always, negatives only when the flag is off.
  _calc_raw_size / _calc_margin divide by abs(price) so a negative entry
  price yields a positive size magnitude (direction carries the sign) and
  positive collateral — unchanged for positive prices. _calc_pnl already
  uses a price difference, well-defined through zero.

Tests open a position on a negative-price bar and assert size/margin/PnL are
well-defined through zero, that an exactly-zero price is still rejected with

fix(backtest): make the buy-and-hold return path sign-safe

close.pct_change() silently assumes price[t-1] > 0. That holds for equities but
not for instruments that can print zero or negative prices, such as European
day-ahead power. As the divisor approaches zero an ordinary absolute move reads
as an enormous percentage move, so the compounded benchmark explodes — a
reported +39,560% where the honest figure was -42.7%. At exactly zero the next
bar is inf, which fillna(0.0) does not neutralise because it fills NaN, and
(1 + r).prod() then collapses to nan.

Adopt an explicit contract. A return is defined only when the previous price is
finite and strictly positive; otherwise it is 0.0, never inf or nan. Buy-and-
hold total return becomes the price relative P_end / P_start - 1 rather than the
compounded product, and is omitted entirely when the entry price is not
positive, because no honest percentage exists. Undefined bars are logged rather
than silently swallowed: a wrong return is a wrong reported number, not a crash.

bar_returns keeps the exact `close / prev - 1` expression pct_change uses, so
results for strictly positive series are bit-identical and ordinary equity and
crypto runs are unchanged.

The loader still rejects an exact-zero close, but the reason has narrowed to the
one that survives: sizing is target_notional / abs(price), undefined at zero.

Closes #872

   this check and appear as additional timeline entries; merge_asof then

fix(ibkr): replace per-call connect/disconnect with thread-safe connection pool

## Problem
The local IBKR connector opened a fresh `ib_async.IB()` connection and
disconnected it on every single tool call (get_account_snapshot,
get_positions, get_open_orders, get_quote, get_historical_bars).  When
the agent invoked multiple trading tools in parallel every call reused
the same hard-coded client ID (77), which caused TWS / IB Gateway to
reject the duplicates with error 326:

    Unable to connect as the client id is already in use.
    Peer closed connection. clientId 77 already in use?

This made the connector unreliable under the agent's parallel execution
model and surfaced as intermittent `TimeOutError` and `Could not
connect to TWS / IB Gateway` errors in the CLI and Web UI.

## Solution
Replace the module-level `_connect()` / `_disconnect()` helpers with
a thread-safe connection pool class `_TwsPool` backed by a
`threading.Lock` and reference counting.

- `_pool.acquire(config)` connects once on first use; subsequent
  concurrent callers reuse the same `ib_async.IB` socket without
  reconnecting.
- `_pool.release()` decrements the refcount; the underlying socket is
  disconnected only when the last active caller releases.
- Guards against mid-flight profile switching (different host / port /
  profile) with a clear error instead of a silent misconfiguration.

All five public functions updated to use `_pool.acquire(cfg)` /
`_pool.release()`.  Call-site contract is unchanged — same
`try: … finally: _pool.release()` pattern.

## Impact
- No more client-ID collision errors under parallel agent call patterns.
- No resource leak from orphaned `ib_async.IB` instances.
- All 10 existing `test_ibkr_local.py` tests pass without modification.

fix(ibkr): restore tick-wait in get_quote and add timing + concurrency tests

## Problem 1: Empty ticker in get_quote (timing regression)

Commit b88df78 changed reqMktData(..., snapshot=True) to avoid the
2-second sleep and thread-safety deadlock, but the ib_async documentation
states: "The ticker will initially be empty and gradually (after a couple
of seconds) be filled" -- even with snapshot mode.  Reading the ticker
fields immediately after reqMktData returned None for bid/ask/last in
production, silently breaking all quote-dependent analysis.

## Problem 2: Existing test hid the bug

The _FakeIB.reqMktData mock returned a fully-populated ticker instantly
(bid=100.0, ask=100.2, ...), so the timing regression never surfaced in
CI.  The existing test_quote_and_history_are_readonly test passed despite
the bug.

## Solution

### agent/src/trading/connectors/ibkr/local.py

- Added _wait_for_tick(ib, ticker) helper that pumps the ib_async event
  loop via ib.waitOnUpdate() in 100 ms increments until at least one of
  bid/ask/last is populated, with a configurable 2-second timeout.
  Falls back to ib.sleep() for ib_async versions without waitOnUpdate.
- get_quote now calls _wait_for_tick() immediately after
  reqMktData(snapshot=True), ensuring the ticker fields are filled
  before serializing the quote response.
- Moved import itertools to the top-level import block (was previously
  added inline before the _TwsPool class in commit b88df78).

### agent/tests/test_ibkr_local.py -- 5 new tests

Timing tests (2):
- test_quote_waits_for_tick_arrival -- mock returns an initially-empty
  ticker; the wait loop runs without hanging, exits gracefully (fields
  stay None if data never arrives -- no deadlock).
- test_quote_receives_tick_after_event_loop_pump -- simulates the real
  async-tick flow: ticker starts empty, after 2 event-loop pumps
  _obj_get is patched to return populated values.  Asserts bid=150.0,
  ask=150.5, last=150.25 are correctly read after the wait loop.

Thread-local pool concurrency tests (3):
- test_pool_thread_local_isolation -- 4 concurrent threads acquire the
  pool via ThreadPoolExecutor with threading.Barrier to force distinct
  worker threads.  Each thread gets a unique client ID (> base 77) and
  a distinct ib_async.IB object.  Verifies no cross-thread leakage.
- test_pool_refcount_disconnects_on_last_release -- nested
  acquire/release in the same thread: disconnect is called only when
  the refcount reaches zero after the final release.
- test_pool_release_idempotent_no_connection -- calling release() on an
  empty pool is a safe no-op.

## Impact

- Quotes now work correctly in production -- ticker fields are populated
  before reading.
- All 10 existing + 5 new = 15 tests pass.
- The wait loop adds ~100-300 ms per quote in the common case (tick
  arrives quickly), with a 2-second safety ceiling.

   engine and the standalone main so every writer of validation.json emits

IndiaEquityEngine imported _calc_pct_change from china_a, which assumes
Tushare's percentage-point convention (5.0 = 5%) and always divides by 100.

fix(llm): preserve Gemini thought_signature through the AgentLoop dict path

#176 added the Gemini thought_signature round-trip but only covered the
in-memory AIMessage path its unit tests exercise. The AgentLoop replays
conversation history as OpenAI-format dicts, stamping the signature into
tool_calls[i].extra_content.google.thought_signature
(loop.py _attach_tool_call_thought_signatures).

LangChain's _convert_dict_to_message discards extra_content during the early
_convert_input step of invoke()/stream() -- before _get_request_payload
re-injects -- so _signature_maps reads an empty additional_kwargs and the
outbound request goes out unsigned. Gemini then rejects the next tool-using
turn with HTTP 400 "Function call is missing a thought_signature in
functionCall parts". This broke every tool-using loop turn on gemini-3.x
(single or parallel), e.g. the parallel load_skill case.

Override ChatOpenAIWithReasoning._convert_input -- the single chokepoint both
invoke and stream call while input is still raw dicts -- to lift signatures
back onto the converted AIMessage in the same
additional_kwargs["tool_call_thought_signatures"] shape the in-memory path
uses, so the existing _signature_maps / _inject_tool_call_thought_signatures
machinery handles both paths identically. Idempotent via an
isinstance(raw, dict) guard. No parallel-specific handling needed: Gemini
signs only the first of N parallel calls and that signature covers the block.

Add regression tests in TestChatOpenAIWithReasoningOutboundPayload that drive
the real dict path (the gap #176's tests missed): red without the fix
(KeyError: 'extra_content'), green with it.

fix(mcp): handle dataclass tool results in _make_jsonable (#849)

_make_jsonable only converted Pydantic BaseModel instances (via
model_dump), list, and dict. fastmcp's client auto-types
CallToolResult.data from a tool's output schema via
json_schema_to_type, which produces a plain stdlib dataclass (not a
BaseModel) whenever the schema doesn't set additionalProperties: true
-- the common case for a typical Pydantic-model tool return type. Such
an instance fell through to the final `return value` unconverted, so
json.dumps's `default` callback received the same unconvertible object
back and raised ValueError: Circular reference detected (its cycle
detector can't distinguish "default() gave up" from an actual cycle).

Adds a dataclasses.is_dataclass branch that recurses per-field (not a
raw asdict(), which would leave nested datetime/dataclass values
unconverted), plus a datetime/date branch, since a date-time schema
field validates to a real datetime object and would hit the same
failure one level down.

Reproduced against the real fastmcp dependency using an MCP tool's
output schema shaped like this (plain object properties, no
additionalProperties, nested datetime field): old _make_jsonable raises
the reported Circular reference detected error; the patched version
serializes correctly, verified both from direct construction and via
pydantic.TypeAdapter validation (the path fastmcp's client actually
uses).

chore(deps): ignore the transitive versions ccxt exact-pins

ccxt does not use ranges — it exact-pins its entire transitive closure. All 23
of those packages that appear in our lock sit at precisely ccxt's pin, with no
mismatches, so none can move until ccxt itself releases, and ccxt 4.5.68 is
already the latest. Any Dependabot PR touching one is unmergeable by
construction: the pip group PR proposed five of them and died with
ResolutionImpossible on certifi against the ccxt line in the lock.

Re-running the resolver confirms this is the ceiling rather than a stale lock —
pip-compile --upgrade under python:3.11-slim, matching CI, reproduces every one
of those versions, so there is no lock change to make. pydantic-core is in the
same position via pydantic's own == pin, and was the sixth package in that PR.

Ignore the set. ccxt itself is deliberately not ignored: it is the package whose
bump legitimately carries all of them. This suppresses only the automated PRs —
Dependabot alerts come from the dependency graph and are unaffected by this
file, so a CVE in cryptography, urllib3, requests or certifi still surfaces in
the Security tab, where the remedy is a ccxt bump.

fix(backtest): keep bar_returns bit-identical for gapped positive series (#895)

* fix(backtest): keep bar_returns bit-identical for gapped positive series

#872 replaced close.pct_change().fillna(0.0) with bar_returns and stated that
results for strictly positive series are bit-identical, so ordinary equity and
crypto runs are unchanged. That was verified only on gapless series.

On the pinned pandas (>=2.0,<3.0) pct_change defaults to fill_method='pad' and
forward-fills the divisor. bar_returns divided by the raw shifted series, so any
positive series with an interior NaN diverged. _align deliberately limits its
ffill to 5 bars (base.py:166-179) to keep long suspensions visible, so a halt
longer than that reaches bar_returns as a NaN prior and the real move across it
is reported as 0.0 -- silently, because the undefined-bar counter excludes NaN
priors by construction. On a real _align run an 8-bar halt turned a +17.1429%
resumed-trading bar into +0.0000%.

Injecting a zero where a large move occurred shrinks dispersion. Return deltas
cancel by sign; that damage does not. On a 20-symbol universe with two halted
symbols and news-shaped gaps, annualised vol fell 4.9619% -> 4.4673% and Sharpe
rose 3.0502 -> 3.3817.

Carry the prior price forward explicitly. This restores the pre-#872 answer and,
unlike the deprecated default it replaces, gives the same result on every
supported pandas -- the old behaviour flips silently under pandas 3.0, where
fill_method is None. The #872 contract is untouched: a non-positive prior is
still undefined, still 0.0, still logged.

Second, smaller item: inf > 0 is True, so where(prev > 0) kept an infinite prior
and the bar after it read as a clean -1.0 with no warning. buy_and_hold_return
had the same asymmetry -- it checked isfinite(last) but only first > 0, so an
infinite entry price returned -100% instead of None. Both now assert finiteness.

fix(fundamentals): dedup restated rows and prevent period regression in PIT snapshots

Two point-in-time correctness bugs in tushare_fundamentals.py:

1. `query_fundamentals` did not deduplicate after the PIT cut, so the same
   (ts_code, end_date) could appear twice when both the original filing and a
   later restatement were visible as of the query date.  Fix: after the PIT
   cut, keep only the row with the latest effective pit date per
   (ts_code, end_date); ties preserve the last row in input order (natural
   Tushare ordering where restatements follow originals).

2. `enrich_price_frames_with_fundamentals` fed the deduped snapshot directly
   into merge_asof.  This caused two problems: (a) the per-day PIT visibility
   was evaluated on already-deduped data, making a restatement whose pit_date
   was in the future appear as if it were always visible; (b) when a late
   restatement for an *older* period (end_date < currently-visible end_date)
   arrived, merge_asof picked it as the nearest-prior announcement, regressing
   every subsequent snapshot to the older period.

   Fix: enrich now calls the new internal `_query_pit_cut` (raw PIT cut, no
   dedup) and builds an explicit forward-only effective timeline — a row is
   only accepted into the timeline when its end_date >= the currently-visible
   end_date.  Same-period restatements (same end_date, later pit_date) pass
   this check and appear as additional timeline entries; merge_asof then
   surfaces the restatement value only from its own pit_date onward.

Fixes #771

Add allow_nonpositive_prices: open on negative-price bars, still reject zero (#816)

Markets like European day-ahead power clear negative routinely, but the
loader's validate_ohlc drops any bar with a non-positive OHLC value and the
engine rejects any open at price <= 0. On real EU power data this silently
deletes ~27% of DE-LU days (every bar with a sub-zero hourly-derived low),
punching holes in rolling statistics (e.g. a z-score entry signal) with no
warning.

Add an opt-in `allow_nonpositive_prices` flag (default False — existing
behavior byte-identical for all positive-price markets):

- loaders/base.py: validate_ohlc gains the flag. Structural invariants
  (high<low, high/low bracketing open/close) always enforced; when the flag
  is set, negative prices pass through and only an exactly-zero price is
  rejected. Zero is genuinely undefined for `size = notional / price` and
  margin; a negative price is well-defined via abs().
- engines/base.py: BaseEngine reads the flag from config. _plan_open_order
  rejects an exactly-zero open always, negatives only when the flag is off.
  _calc_raw_size / _calc_margin divide by abs(price) so a negative entry
  price yields a positive size magnitude (direction carries the sign) and
  positive collateral — unchanged for positive prices. _calc_pnl already
  uses a price difference, well-defined through zero.

Tests open a position on a negative-price bar and assert size/margin/PnL are
well-defined through zero, that an exactly-zero price is still rejected with
the flag on, and that the default still rejects negatives. A regression test
pins *why* zero stays dropped rather than kept: a surviving 0.00 close yields
inf at the `close.pct_change().fillna(0.0)` sites in benchmark.py and
engines/base.py (fillna fills NaN, not inf), so keeping it would corrupt the
return series. Fixture carries the 5 real non-positive-close bars from a 2025
NO2/DE-LU window (ENTSO-E via Energy-Charts / Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD,
CC BY 4.0). Existing engine and OHLC-validation suites pass unchanged
(140 tests total).

fix(swarm): block downstream tasks when upstream fails

Bug
---
A failed task in layer N did NOT prevent layer N+1 tasks that declare it
as a dependency from being dispatched. The orchestration loop in
_execute_run set all_succeeded=False on failure but never gated the next
layer. The downstream worker's upstream-summary loop in _execute_layer
silently skipped the missing key (the `if source_task_id in task_summaries`
check), so the worker ran with no upstream context.

This is most visible in the investment_committee preset, where
portfolio_manager depends_on=["task-risk"]: a failed risk_officer
let PM produce a "decision" with no risk input. Reproducer attached as
tests/test_swarm_dag_gating.py shows the same pattern in 3 tasks.

The layer-boundary _sync_run_tasks_snapshot added in #132 surfaces the
failure to polling clients sooner, but it does not gate dispatch — PM
still runs the moment the layer with the failed risk task finishes.

Fix
---
_execute_layer: before dispatch, walk task.depends_on and load each
  upstream from TaskStore. If any upstream has status != completed
  (failed / blocked / cancelled / missing), mark this task
  TaskStatus.blocked, record blocked_by + reason, emit task_blocked,
  and skip executor.submit. Same-layer peers with no shared upstream
  are unaffected (the loop continues).

_execute_run: tasks blocked in _execute_layer are absent from
  layer_results. After the result loop, any layer_task_id missing from
  layer_results was blocked -> set all_succeeded = False so the run is
  marked RunStatus.failed at finalization.

Tests
-----
3 new regression tests in tests/test_swarm_dag_gating.py (TDD red-green
verified before-and-after on this PR's diff):
  - test_failed_upstream_blocks_downstream
  - test_blocked_downstream_emits_task_blocked_event
  - test_run_marked_failed_when_downstream_blocked

feat(swarm): pre-fetch market data and ground worker prompts in real prices

Symptom
-------
Workers in fundamental_research_team and similar presets routinely quote
prices from their model's training cutoff. A run targeting NVDA.US in
2026-05 produced a research report anchored on $145.89 while the actual
yfinance close that day was $215.20. Subsequent recommendations
("Hold/Accumulate, target $148-160") were therefore wrong by 30%+ before
any analyst even saw them. issue #42-class "weird outputs" land here too
when a worker silently substitutes a remembered number for a missing
data call.

Why prompt rules alone don't fix it
-----------------------------------
worker.py:158-171 already prints generic "use tools when needed"
guidance. LLMs nevertheless prefer the cheap path of recalling a number
over the expensive path of issuing a tool call — especially under the
20-tool-call hard limit imposed two paragraphs later. Adding a stronger
"never quote prices" rule helps but does not eliminate the failure mode.

Fix
---
Make the data unavoidable. SwarmRuntime.start_run now:

  1. Scans every value in user_vars for suffixed symbols
     (NVDA.US / 700.HK / 600519.SH / BTC-USDT / 000001.SZ / 430090.BJ).
  2. Pre-fetches the last 30 days of OHLCV via the existing loader
     registry (resolve_loader handles per-market routing). Failures
     are non-fatal — the run still proceeds, just without grounding.
  3. Pins the result on a new SwarmRun.grounding_data field and
     persists it via the existing run.json path.

SwarmRuntime._execute_run renders the data into a markdown "Ground
Truth" block once per run and threads it through
_run_worker_with_retries -> run_worker -> build_worker_prompt, which
splices it ahead of Execution Rules. The block contains the recent
window range, last close, the last 5 daily closes, and an explicit
instruction to prefer these prices over training-data prices and to
call get_market_data for any range outside the window.

Backward compatibility
----------------------
* SwarmRun.grounding_data defaults to None; existing run.json files
  parse unchanged (Pydantic deserialises the missing key to the
  default). The legacy regression case is covered by
  test_swarm_run_metadata.py once that lands; this PR's tests cover the
  new module and prompt plumbing in isolation.
* build_worker_prompt and run_worker each gain a grounding_block= kw
  with default "" so callers outside the swarm runtime keep working.
* Empty grounding (no symbols detected, or every fetch failed) skips
  the entire section — no empty heading rendered.

What's not in scope
-------------------
* Bare tickers without a suffix (just "NVDA") are intentionally not
  matched. The false-positive cost on common English words is too high
  and every shipped preset already supplies suffixed symbols.
* The block is a one-shot snapshot at run start. Long-running swarms
  may see stale data after many minutes — still strictly better than
  training-data prices from a year ago. A refresh hook can land later.

Tests
-----
agent/tests/test_swarm_grounding.py covers symbol extraction (all four
loader-supported suffix shapes, ordering, non-string values, word
boundaries), fetch behaviour with a stubbed loader (normalised bars,
empty-frame skip, empty-input no-op), markdown rendering (range / last
close / explicit instruction text), and end-to-end prompt plumbing
(grounding block lands before Execution Rules; absent block omits the
section). All 12 pass; full pytest sweep against main shows the same
pre-existing 3 failures (test_backtest_runner_security x2,
test_loop_helpers normalize) as main and 875 passed (= baseline 863 +
the new 12 grounding tests).

fix(ibkr): replace per-call connect/disconnect with thread-safe connection pool

## Problem
The local IBKR connector opened a fresh `ib_async.IB()` connection and
disconnected it on every single tool call (get_account_snapshot,
get_positions, get_open_orders, get_quote, get_historical_bars).  When
the agent invoked multiple trading tools in parallel every call reused
the same hard-coded client ID (77), which caused TWS / IB Gateway to
reject the duplicates with error 326:

    Unable to connect as the client id is already in use.
    Peer closed connection. clientId 77 already in use?

This made the connector unreliable under the agent's parallel execution
model and surfaced as intermittent `TimeOutError` and `Could not
connect to TWS / IB Gateway` errors in the CLI and Web UI.

## Solution
Replace the module-level `_connect()` / `_disconnect()` helpers with
a thread-safe connection pool class `_TwsPool` backed by a
`threading.Lock` and reference counting.

- `_pool.acquire(config)` connects once on first use; subsequent
  concurrent callers reuse the same `ib_async.IB` socket without
  reconnecting.
- `_pool.release()` decrements the refcount; the underlying socket is
  disconnected only when the last active caller releases.
- Guards against mid-flight profile switching (different host / port /
  profile) with a clear error instead of a silent misconfiguration.

All five public functions updated to use `_pool.acquire(cfg)` /
`_pool.release()`.  Call-site contract is unchanged — same
`try: … finally: _pool.release()` pattern.

fix(security): block CGNAT/mesh ranges in SSRF guard; close QQ media redirect-to-internal

Two SSRF gaps in the channel media-fetch path:

1. channels/utils._is_private only checked is_loopback | is_link_local |
   is_private. ipaddress.is_private is False for RFC 6598 shared address
   space (100.64.0.0/10 — the default Tailscale/mesh range), so those hosts
   passed validate_url_target and every channel (QQ, DingTalk, NapCat,
   Telegram, channelsui) would fetch them as media. Switch to
   `not addr.is_global or addr.is_multicast`, which blocks all
   non-globally-routable ranges uniformly and also closes an IPv4-multicast
   gap (is_global is True for multicast). Matches web_reader_tool._url_allowed.

2. qq._read_media_bytes validated media_ref once, then fetched with
   allow_redirects=True. media_ref is agent-controlled (from msg.media, which
   is routinely influenced by untrusted external content), so a public URL
   returning 302 -> http://169.254.169.254/... would be followed unchecked and
   the internal body uploaded as a media attachment. Set allow_redirects=False
   and fail closed on 3xx, mirroring napcat.py. (The separate inbound download
   at qq.py:618 fetches a trusted QQ CDN URL and is intentionally left as-is.)

Adds agent/tests/test_url_target_security.py covering both fixes. The central
guard (validate_url_target / _is_private) previously had no tests at all.

fix(backtest): make the buy-and-hold return path sign-safe

close.pct_change() silently assumes price[t-1] > 0. That holds for equities but
not for instruments that can print zero or negative prices, such as European
day-ahead power. As the divisor approaches zero an ordinary absolute move reads
as an enormous percentage move, so the compounded benchmark explodes — a
reported +39,560% where the honest figure was -42.7%. At exactly zero the next
bar is inf, which fillna(0.0) does not neutralise because it fills NaN, and
(1 + r).prod() then collapses to nan.

Adopt an explicit contract. A return is defined only when the previous price is
finite and strictly positive; otherwise it is 0.0, never inf or nan. Buy-and-
hold total return becomes the price relative P_end / P_start - 1 rather than the
compounded product, and is omitted entirely when the entry price is not
positive, because no honest percentage exists. Undefined bars are logged rather
than silently swallowed: a wrong return is a wrong reported number, not a crash.

bar_returns keeps the exact `close / prev - 1` expression pct_change uses, so
results for strictly positive series are bit-identical and ordinary equity and
crypto runs are unchanged.

The loader still rejects an exact-zero close, but the reason has narrowed to the
one that survives: sizing is target_notional / abs(price), undefined at zero.

fix(shadow): skip the entry-hour gate on daily bars

Rules mined from real journals carry an entry_hour window from actual
fill times (p10-p90, e.g. 9-11 for market-hours trading). The generated
signal engine replays on daily bars stamped at midnight, so gating on
bar_hour rejected every bar: any profile mined from real intraday fills
produced a silently flat strategy with zero entries and no error.

information, so the generated engine now applies it only when the bar
index has more than one distinct time-of-day (intraday data). Other
rule conditions (RSI, prior return, holding) are unchanged.

bars, intraday data still enforcing the window, and date-only journal

fix(ibkr): replace fixed 2s sleep with ib.sleep() polling loop that exits on real data

The single ib.sleep(2.0) call in _wait_for_tick was unreliable when
multiple quotes ran in parallel via ThreadPoolExecutor (8 workers).
Each thread has its own IB connection (thread-local pool), but the
fixed 2s sleep doesn't account for varying network latency -- some
ticks arrive in 200ms, others take longer, and 2s wasn't always
enough, causing empty/NaN fields in 7/10 parallel quote requests.

Replace with incremental ib.sleep(0.1) polling that checks
_tick_has_data after each pump and exits as soon as real market data
arrives, with a 5s total timeout. This gives each ticker dedicated
event-loop time and avoids the race where the LLM reads partial data.

Key: uses ib.sleep() NOT waitOnUpdate() for polling -- ib.sleep
reliably processes all pending socket messages, while waitOnUpdate
can return True for unrelated messages on the same connection.

Changes:
- Re-add _tick_has_data() with None + NaN rejection
- Rewrite _wait_for_tick() as ib.sleep(0.1) polling loop (5s timeout)
- Add test_quote_waits_for_delayed_tick_arrival: tick arrives after
  5 pump cycles, verifies correct bid/ask/last values

fix(optimizers): exclude decision-bar returns (#487)

BaseOptimizer.optimize() built each estimation window with ret.loc[:dt], which
includes ret[dt] — a close-to-close return for the decision date. Since
weights at dt execute at that bar's open, ret[dt] isn't actually observable
yet at execution time, so every optimizer built on this base (mean-variance,
equal-volatility, max-diversification, risk-parity, turnover-aware) was
leaking one bar of future information into its own decision.

Fix restricts the window to ret.index < dt. Two regression tests prove it:
the window's latest timestamp always precedes the decision date, and shocking
only the decision-bar return leaves that bar's executed weights unchanged.
Backtests without an optimizer are unaffected; this does change historical
optimized results as intended (removing a look-ahead leak, not introducing
one).

calc_metrics computed the annualised return as

computation (and the backtest run reporting it).

runs are unchanged. Adds regression tests for a zero-equity wipeout and a

test: make path-handling tests pass on Windows runners

Three tests fail when the suite is run on Windows even though the
underlying behaviour is correct on both platforms — the failures are
test-side platform assumptions, not application bugs. Linux CI is
unaffected; this is purely a quality-of-life fix for contributors who
run pytest on Windows.

1. test_backtest_runner_security.py — rce path interpolation
   ----------------------------------------------------------
   Both ``test_signal_engine_rejects_top_level_execution`` and
   ``test_signal_engine_rejects_class_level_execution`` write a
   ``signal_engine.py`` whose source contains the pytest tmp_path
   formatted into an ``os.system('touch ...')`` call. On Windows,
   tmp_path looks like ``C:\Users\teera\AppData\Local\Temp\...``;
   interpolated into a single-quoted Python string literal, the leading
   ``\U`` is interpreted as a (truncated) unicode escape and ``ast.parse``
   raises ``SyntaxError`` before the security scrubber under test ever
   runs. Switching to ``Path.as_posix()`` produces forward-slash paths
   that survive Python source escaping intact while pointing at the same
   filesystem location on every OS.

2. test_loop_helpers.py — absolute-path preservation
   --------------------------------------------------
   ``test_preserves_absolute_run_dir`` passed the literal
   ``/var/tmp/custom_run`` and expected it back unchanged.
   ``_normalize_tool_run_dir`` calls ``Path.is_absolute()``, which on
   Windows returns False for a bare drive-less path — so the function
   correctly treats the input as relative and joins it with
   ``memory_run_dir``. The test was wrong, not the function: it asserted
   POSIX semantics on a cross-platform helper. Resolving the input
   through ``os.path.abspath`` before handing it to the function
   produces the platform's actual absolute form (``/var/tmp/custom_run``
   on POSIX, ``C:\var\tmp\custom_run`` on Windows) and the assertion now
   holds on both.

Verified locally: the targeted three now pass; the full pytest sweep
goes from "3 failed, 863 passed" on main to "866 passed, 0 failed".

fix(anthropic): self-heal models that deprecate the temperature field (#890)

Problem
-------
Next-gen Claude models (e.g. claude-opus-5, claude-opus-4-8, claude-sonnet-5)
reject the "temperature" request field with HTTP 400 "temperature is deprecated
for this model." for ANY value, while older models (claude-opus-4-5,
claude-sonnet-4-5, ...) still accept it. _build_anthropic unconditionally
forwarded the global default temperature=0.0, so every run on a next-gen model
failed before producing output. Model names are not predictable (opus-4-5
accepts it, opus-4-8 does not) and the rejection is value-independent, so
neither a fixed model allowlist nor an "omit when 0.0" shortcut is a correct
fix.

Solution
--------
Add a temperature-safe ChatAnthropic subclass (_make_temperature_safe_anthropic)
that wraps all four generation entry points (_generate, _agenerate, _stream,
_astream). When the API reports temperature as unsupported it drops the field
and retries once, then records the model in a process-wide set so subsequent
requests omit it up front (no repeated failed request). Models that accept
temperature keep their configured deterministic value unchanged. The subclass
is built from the lazily-imported class and cached per base class, preserving
the optional langchain-anthropic dependency boundary and existing test doubles.

Correct for any temperature value, current and future model names, and the
streaming path the Web UI relies on.

Tests
-----
Add regression tests in agent/tests/test_llm.py: self-heal retry drops
temperature and remembers the model, temperature is preserved for supporting
models, and the error matcher only triggers on temperature-unsupported errors.
Full test_llm.py suite: 58 passed.

fix(mcp): handle dataclass tool results in _make_jsonable (#849)

_make_jsonable only converted Pydantic BaseModel instances (via
model_dump), list, and dict. fastmcp's client auto-types
CallToolResult.data from a tool's output schema via
json_schema_to_type, which produces a plain stdlib dataclass (not a
BaseModel) whenever the schema doesn't set additionalProperties: true
-- the common case for a typical Pydantic-model tool return type. Such
an instance fell through to the final `return value` unconverted, so
json.dumps's `default` callback received the same unconvertible object
back and raised ValueError: Circular reference detected (its cycle
detector can't distinguish "default() gave up" from an actual cycle).

Adds a dataclasses.is_dataclass branch that recurses per-field (not a
raw asdict(), which would leave nested datetime/dataclass values
unconverted), plus a datetime/date branch, since a date-time schema
field validates to a real datetime object and would hit the same
failure one level down.

Reproduced against the real fastmcp dependency using an MCP tool's
output schema shaped like this (plain object properties, no
additionalProperties, nested datetime field): old _make_jsonable raises
the reported Circular reference detected error; the patched version
serializes correctly, verified both from direct construction and via
pydantic.TypeAdapter validation (the path fastmcp's client actually
uses).

fix(fundamentals): dedup restated rows and prevent period regression in PIT snapshots

Two point-in-time correctness bugs in tushare_fundamentals.py:

1. `query_fundamentals` did not deduplicate after the PIT cut, so the same
   (ts_code, end_date) could appear twice when both the original filing and a
   later restatement were visible as of the query date.  Fix: after the PIT
   cut, keep only the row with the latest effective pit date per
   (ts_code, end_date); ties preserve the last row in input order (natural
   Tushare ordering where restatements follow originals).

2. `enrich_price_frames_with_fundamentals` fed the deduped snapshot directly
   into merge_asof.  This caused two problems: (a) the per-day PIT visibility
   was evaluated on already-deduped data, making a restatement whose pit_date
   was in the future appear as if it were always visible; (b) when a late
   restatement for an *older* period (end_date < currently-visible end_date)
   arrived, merge_asof picked it as the nearest-prior announcement, regressing
   every subsequent snapshot to the older period.

   Fix: enrich now calls the new internal `_query_pit_cut` (raw PIT cut, no
   dedup) and builds an explicit forward-only effective timeline — a row is
   only accepted into the timeline when its end_date >= the currently-visible
   end_date.  Same-period restatements (same end_date, later pit_date) pass
   this check and appear as additional timeline entries; merge_asof then
   surfaces the restatement value only from its own pit_date onward.

Fixes #771

fix(backtest): validate validation-config knobs instead of crashing

The three validation tools read count/seed knobs straight from user
config["validation"] via run_validation, but none validated them:

  - walk_forward n_windows=0  -> ZeroDivisionError (len // n_windows)
  - walk_forward n_windows<0  -> silently returns empty windows with a
                                 NaN return_mean and negative consistency_rate
  - monte_carlo n_simulations<1 -> ZeroDivisionError (count / n_simulations)
  - monte_carlo/bootstrap seed<0 -> ValueError from np.random.default_rng
  - bootstrap n_bootstrap<1   -> IndexError from np.percentile on empty array
  - bootstrap confidence outside (0,1) -> ValueError from np.percentile

A single misconfigured knob either aborted the whole backtest with an
opaque error or returned NaN-laden garbage with no signal. Guard each knob
at function entry and return the same {"error": ...} shape these functions
already use for insufficient data, so a bad knob surfaces cleanly in the
validation results instead of crashing or silently corrupting the run.

fix(shadow): skip the entry-hour gate on daily bars

fill times (p10-p90, e.g. 9-11 for market-hours trading). The generated

Add allow_nonpositive_prices: open on negative-price bars, still reject zero (#816)

Markets like European day-ahead power clear negative routinely, but the
loader's validate_ohlc drops any bar with a non-positive OHLC value and the
engine rejects any open at price <= 0. On real EU power data this silently
deletes ~27% of DE-LU days (every bar with a sub-zero hourly-derived low),
punching holes in rolling statistics (e.g. a z-score entry signal) with no
warning.

Add an opt-in `allow_nonpositive_prices` flag (default False — existing
behavior byte-identical for all positive-price markets):

- loaders/base.py: validate_ohlc gains the flag. Structural invariants
  (high<low, high/low bracketing open/close) always enforced; when the flag
  is set, negative prices pass through and only an exactly-zero price is
  rejected. Zero is genuinely undefined for `size = notional / price` and
  margin; a negative price is well-defined via abs().
- engines/base.py: BaseEngine reads the flag from config. _plan_open_order
  rejects an exactly-zero open always, negatives only when the flag is off.
  _calc_raw_size / _calc_margin divide by abs(price) so a negative entry
  price yields a positive size magnitude (direction carries the sign) and
  positive collateral — unchanged for positive prices. _calc_pnl already
  uses a price difference, well-defined through zero.

Tests open a position on a negative-price bar and assert size/margin/PnL are
well-defined through zero, that an exactly-zero price is still rejected with
the flag on, and that the default still rejects negatives. A regression test
pins *why* zero stays dropped rather than kept: a surviving 0.00 close yields
inf at the `close.pct_change().fillna(0.0)` sites in benchmark.py and
engines/base.py (fillna fills NaN, not inf), so keeping it would corrupt the
return series. Fixture carries the 5 real non-positive-close bars from a 2025
NO2/DE-LU window (ENTSO-E via Energy-Charts / Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD,
CC BY 4.0). Existing engine and OHLC-validation suites pass unchanged
(140 tests total).

fix(mcp): handle dataclass tool results in _make_jsonable (#849)

_make_jsonable only converted Pydantic BaseModel instances (via
model_dump), list, and dict. fastmcp's client auto-types
CallToolResult.data from a tool's output schema via
json_schema_to_type, which produces a plain stdlib dataclass (not a
BaseModel) whenever the schema doesn't set additionalProperties: true
-- the common case for a typical Pydantic-model tool return type. Such
an instance fell through to the final `return value` unconverted, so
json.dumps's `default` callback received the same unconvertible object
back and raised ValueError: Circular reference detected (its cycle
detector can't distinguish "default() gave up" from an actual cycle).

Adds a dataclasses.is_dataclass branch that recurses per-field (not a
raw asdict(), which would leave nested datetime/dataclass values
unconverted), plus a datetime/date branch, since a date-time schema
field validates to a real datetime object and would hit the same
failure one level down.

Reproduced against the real fastmcp dependency using an MCP tool's
output schema shaped like this (plain object properties, no
additionalProperties, nested datetime field): old _make_jsonable raises
the reported Circular reference detected error; the patched version
serializes correctly, verified both from direct construction and via
pydantic.TypeAdapter validation (the path fastmcp's client actually
uses).

fix(backtest): keep bar_returns bit-identical for gapped positive series (#895)

* fix(backtest): keep bar_returns bit-identical for gapped positive series

#872 replaced close.pct_change().fillna(0.0) with bar_returns and stated that
results for strictly positive series are bit-identical, so ordinary equity and
crypto runs are unchanged. That was verified only on gapless series.

On the pinned pandas (>=2.0,<3.0) pct_change defaults to fill_method='pad' and
forward-fills the divisor. bar_returns divided by the raw shifted series, so any
positive series with an interior NaN diverged. _align deliberately limits its
ffill to 5 bars (base.py:166-179) to keep long suspensions visible, so a halt
longer than that reaches bar_returns as a NaN prior and the real move across it
is reported as 0.0 -- silently, because the undefined-bar counter excludes NaN
priors by construction. On a real _align run an 8-bar halt turned a +17.1429%
resumed-trading bar into +0.0000%.

Injecting a zero where a large move occurred shrinks dispersion. Return deltas
cancel by sign; that damage does not. On a 20-symbol universe with two halted
symbols and news-shaped gaps, annualised vol fell 4.9619% -> 4.4673% and Sharpe
rose 3.0502 -> 3.3817.

Carry the prior price forward explicitly. This restores the pre-#872 answer and,
unlike the deprecated default it replaces, gives the same result on every
supported pandas -- the old behaviour flips silently under pandas 3.0, where
fill_method is None. The #872 contract is untouched: a non-positive prior is
still undefined, still 0.0, still logged.

Second, smaller item: inf > 0 is True, so where(prev > 0) kept an infinite prior
and the bar after it read as a clean -1.0 with no warning. buy_and_hold_return
had the same asymmetry -- it checked isfinite(last) but only first > 0, so an
infinite entry price returned -100% instead of None. Both now assert finiteness.

fix(anthropic): self-heal models that deprecate the temperature field (#890)

Problem
-------
Next-gen Claude models (e.g. claude-opus-5, claude-opus-4-8, claude-sonnet-5)
reject the "temperature" request field with HTTP 400 "temperature is deprecated
for this model." for ANY value, while older models (claude-opus-4-5,
claude-sonnet-4-5, ...) still accept it. _build_anthropic unconditionally
forwarded the global default temperature=0.0, so every run on a next-gen model
failed before producing output. Model names are not predictable (opus-4-5
accepts it, opus-4-8 does not) and the rejection is value-independent, so
neither a fixed model allowlist nor an "omit when 0.0" shortcut is a correct
fix.

Solution
--------
Add a temperature-safe ChatAnthropic subclass (_make_temperature_safe_anthropic)
that wraps all four generation entry points (_generate, _agenerate, _stream,
_astream). When the API reports temperature as unsupported it drops the field
and retries once, then records the model in a process-wide set so subsequent
requests omit it up front (no repeated failed request). Models that accept
temperature keep their configured deterministic value unchanged. The subclass
is built from the lazily-imported class and cached per base class, preserving
the optional langchain-anthropic dependency boundary and existing test doubles.

Correct for any temperature value, current and future model names, and the
streaming path the Web UI relies on.

Tests
-----
Add regression tests in agent/tests/test_llm.py: self-heal retry drops
temperature and remembers the model, temperature is preserved for supporting
models, and the error matcher only triggers on temperature-unsupported errors.
Full test_llm.py suite: 58 passed.
